name: Siemens
headline: A industrial group whose factory-automation, grid and medical-technology businesses earn high returns.
what_it_does: Siemens runs factory automation and industrial software (Digital Industries), electrical grid and building technology (Smart Infrastructure), and a majority stake of 67% to 79% in medical-technology maker Healthineers. Over FY2021 to FY2025, these three parts produced 34%, 29% and 28% of its industrial segment profit. The US-traded shares are depositary shares, each representing half of one Siemens ordinary share.
why_it_passed: The largest part's position has stood for a full decade against a named rival's own filings.
Its operations earn high returns on the capital they need and reinvest little to grow.
Smart Infrastructure's segment profit rose from 1,743 million euros in FY2021 to 4,506 million in FY2025.
No doubt about the honesty of present management arose; legacy proceedings from 1992 to 2011 are recorded.
why_not_now: The analysis's central value range is EUR 127.03 to 237.70 per US-traded share (about USD 142 to 266, at an exchange rate it flagged as approximate), against a price of USD 153.36. The price does not clear the framework's bar: the best case earns about 6% a year, and no growth about 3.6%, against about 10% required. The 30-year euro rate is 3.78%.
watch: Digital Industries' segment profit fell from 4,947 million euros in FY2023 to 2,643 million in FY2025, and the analysis flagged the narrowing and an AI threat to its software half.
It has made serial acquisitions at full prices (such as Altair and Dotmatics in 2025) that have not yet shown a decent return, and its 2026 buyback was above the bottom of the value range.
It features an adjusted profit figure and gives earnings guidance.
